sanskrit: यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः । तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम ॥
hindiTranslation: जहाँ योगेश्वर भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण हैं और जहाँ गाण्डीवधनुषधारी अर्जुन हैं, वहाँ ही श्री, विजय, विभूति और अचल नीति है  ऐसा मेरा मत है ॥
englishTranslation: Where Krishna, the master of yoga, is present, and where Arjuna, the bow-bearer, is present, there are prosperity, victory, glory, and firm justice. This is my conviction.
essence: Right action carries its own victory.
speaker: Sanjaya
simpleMeaning: Sanjaya says that wherever Krishna and Arjuna are together, success, prosperity, and right order are assured.
simpleInsight: Where wisdom and committed action stand together, success and right order follow.
detailedMeaning: Sanjaya is closing the Gita for Dhritarashtra. After witnessing Krishna’s teaching and Arjuna’s change of heart, he gives his final judgment: wherever Krishna and Arjuna stand together, that side has the force of truth, victory, and stability.
modernRelevance: In a family business, the elder brother knows the trade and the younger one does the hard selling, and the shop does well. Sanjaya's closing line names a larger version: where Krishna and Arjuna are together, victory follows.
translationLiteral: यत्र (where) / योगेश्वरः (master of yoga) / कृष्णः (Krishna) / यत्र (where) / पार्थः (Arjuna, son of Pritha) / धनुर्धरः (bow-bearer) / तत्र (there) / श्रीः (prosperity, grace) / विजयः (victory) / भूतिः (glory, power) / ध्रुवा (firm, steadfast) / नीतिः (right order, justice) / मम (my)
insight: Sanjaya's closing verdict: where Krishna and Arjuna stand together, prosperity, victory, glory and justice follow.

quoteVariants.text: Where Krishna and Arjuna stand, victory and right order stand too.
Krishna and Arjuna: victory, order, prosperity.
Right order follows where Krishna and Arjuna stand.
